Scene: player stands firmly on a grassy rock path close to, but safely back from, the rim of a lush floating island high above a broken sea of clouds. Immediate foreground is solid ground, wild grasses, a few tiny flowers, damp stone and a small outcrop of naturally embedded mana crystal. Other enormous floating landmasses rise across open sky: suspended rock undersides with deep foundational crystal veins, lush vegetation above, long waterfalls dissolving into mist far below without touching the earth. No constructed bridges between the islands, no ruined temples, no city. A single adult Flying Leviathan drifts about 100 metres off the island, calmly flying horizontally belly down through a gap between islands, shown in a readable three-quarter side view. Exact creature anatomy: an 80-metre-long whale-like body, blunt broad whale head with wide mouthline, deep chest, tapering tail ending in a HORIZONTAL fluke; NO LEGS. One pair of enormous WING-FINS grows from the shoulders, overall span about 110 metres, and an additional pair of much SMALLER pectoral steering fins sits farther FORWARD along the flanks, four fin appendages total plus the horizontal tail fluke. Its wings are marine fleshy fins rather than bat or dragon wings, with no finger-bone webbing, no feathers. Pale blue and pearl-grey upper skin, faintly luminous underside with subtle constellation-like mana markings. Small mana crystals near throat, spine and fins, very restrained glow; no neon outline. Clouds part around its brow, a few tiny birds draft alongside for scale. No saddle or buildings on this wild specimen. Its enormous width has room in the frame and it feels part of the sky rather than a close-up monster. Soft morning sunlight, fresh greens and pearl whites, natural blue sky, incredible height and serene wonder. Player's left gloved hand loosely holds a coil of climbing rope very low at bottom left, occupying less than 5 percent of the image.

Scene: first-person player on the drenched wooden deck of a substantial medieval sailing vessel far out in the Deep Ocean during a severe storm, with no land or safe harbour in sight. Standing player eye level, deck and rails close enough to touch, stout timber mast, functional rigging, rain-dark sailcloth and pitching ink-blue waves. A Kraken is seizing the vessel; its BODY remains entirely submerged and must NOT emerge like a dinosaur or stand upright. Only portions are seen, making the ocean itself feel occupied: three huge muscular blue-black sucker-lined arms rise from the sea, one fresh wet arm flung across the far deck railing before gripping, another curling around a mast, one farther out slipping beneath the water. Do not show the full ten-appendage creature because most is below the surface. The visible arms are about 1.5 metres thick near their base, scarred and mineral-crusted with small shell growths and tangled old ropes; natural biological arms, no serpentine heads. One enormous dark eye about 1.5 metres across is visible just at the sea surface beyond the starboard rail, attached to an indistinct submerged mass under the waves; no separate floating eyeball and no exposed beak. Faint blue bioluminescent lines under the hide, very subtle. A lean feeding tentacle with a broad hooked terminal pad hovers in the middle distance above the deck, the warning before a grab. Around eight adult crew members in practical wet wool and leather clothing act with purpose: several chopping the arm with axes, one readying a hand-thrown barbed harpoon, others hauling rope or steadying themselves. No cannons, guns, modern machinery or tricorn pirate costumes. Player's small right gloved hand holds a plain boarding axe low at bottom right and left hand grips a taut wet safety rope at bottom left. Strong diagonal rain, white foam, dim cold storm daylight and a few warm hooded lanterns, high tension, navigable space between the player's viewpoint and the fighting crew, detailed water and wet materials. No gore, no gore splatter on screen, no huge cinematic explosion, no sky-filling monster portrait.

Scene: a first-person traveller halfway across a narrow, solid ancient stone bridge spanning a deep snowy mountain ravine, approaching the deep gate of a dwarven mountain hold cut directly into an immense cliff. This is a mountain travel scene, not a city interior. Foreground shows snow-dusted flagstones with patches of exposed rough grip stone, heavy waist-high stone parapets and a few old iron anchor rings. The bridge is structurally sound and clearly walkable, with the drop visible safely beyond the parapet. A handful of adult fellow travellers wearing thick wool cloaks with practical packs and an ordinary pack mule proceed ahead toward shelter; one sturdy guard waits beneath the heavy gate. Entrance architecture is functional, monumental, defensive stonework with stout metal-banded doors and a small warm forge-lit or torch-lit vestibule, no giant statues or named heraldry. Towering snow-capped peaks, wind-scoured cliffs and layered ranges behind; exposed switchback path and an isolated stone watchtower on a distant spur provide readable scale. A gust blows fine loose snow across the bridge, frost clings to near masonry, pale cold daylight breaks through thinning cloud while a warm point of light in the gate marks safety. Mountains are enormous and the fortified entrance is impressive but not an entire impossible castle glued to a cliff. Player's thick wool sleeve and small leather-gloved left hand on the parapet at lower left, right hand carrying a plain wood walking staff low at lower right, foreground gear less than 10 percent of image. Realistic cold atmosphere and physical survival travel, no monsters, no dragons, no combat, no magic particles, no fantasy sky spectacle.

Scene: first-person player has paused on a damp narrow ground path amid a dense towering bamboo jungle after rain. Strong slender green and yellow bamboo stalks form vertical corridors, ferns and wet leaf litter underfoot, small root crossings and light mist, diffused pale canopy light with a few warm shafts. In the far middle distance a tiny elevated local village of just two or three huts on stilts, lashed bamboo platforms and one suspended footbridge stands above flood-prone ground; faint cook smoke, not a sprawling city. The central discovery is a BAMBOO SPIDER camouflaged above the path about 12 metres ahead. Exact anatomy: a compact two-part dark mottled spider body hangs in overhead foliage roughly 6 metres above the ground; eight extremely long jointed green-yellow bamboo-mimicking legs, about 7 metres each, ALL attached to the smaller FRONT body segment, four legs each side. Each leg angles UP from the front body then bends sharply DOWN to plant on the ground like a bamboo stalk. Large rear abdomen separate from front segment. Keep the eight thin legs biologically articulated and distinguishable among real bamboo, no extra pincer arms, no front mantis scythes, no human shape, no head on a snake neck. Pale fibrous tendrils are tightly coiled beneath the compact body; do not show a tangled mess or web filling the scene. The body is partly obscured by leaves but enough of it and its attached legs are visible to let the viewer recognise the threatening shape. Natural camouflage rather than bright monster colouring: at first look a peaceful bamboo trail, on second look something has planted its legs around the route. No attack in progress. Player's right gloved hand holds a modest plain iron short sword lowered at bottom right, occupying less than 7 percent of frame. Wet bamboo joints, small reflective puddles, layered natural foliage, lived-in but thinly settled frontier, quiet tension rather than action-poster composition. No gore, no corpse, no giant eyes staring directly into camera, no neon.
